comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C4 regarding lncDach1-dystrophin binding. Both evaluations find the binding data convincing and well-supported by multiple methodologies (RNA pulldown, RIP). OpenEval emphasizes technical controls while peer reviewers highlight this as a key strength with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on claims C5-C13 regarding protein redistribution and localization changes. Both evaluations support the findings showing dystrophin and Nav1.5 redistribution from membrane to intracellular compartments. OpenEval details the multiple techniques used while peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'convincing.'

Perfect agreement on claims C14-C16 regarding electrophysiological effects. Both evaluations support the findings of reduced INa and slower conduction velocity. OpenEval emphasizes the preserved kinetics indicating a trafficking mechanism, while peer reviewers confirm the correspondence between cellular and whole-heart measurements.

Perfect agreement on claims C17-C28 regarding in vitro validation in cultured cardiomyocytes. Both evaluations support the reproducibility of findings in isolated cells infected with adenoviral constructs. OpenEval highlights convergent evidence across techniques while peer reviewers explicitly confirm the INa reduction in isolated cardiomyocytes.

Strong agreement on claims C29-C35 regarding knockout loss-of-function studies. Both evaluations emphasize the bidirectional validation showing opposite phenotypes in knockout versus overexpression. OpenEval focuses on the molecular data while peer reviewers highlight the increased INa and conduction velocity as key reciprocal findings. Peer review R5 also includes claims C36-C38 which OpenEval addresses separately in R6.

Agreement on claims C36-C38 regarding functional consequences in knockout mice. OpenEval evaluates these electrophysiological claims separately while peer reviewers group them with the broader knockout phenotype (C29-C38). Both support the increased INa and preserved kinetics findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C39-C50 regarding in vitro knockdown validation. Both evaluations support the shRNA knockdown experiments showing opposite effects to overexpression. OpenEval emphasizes consistency between shRNA and genetic knockout while peer reviewers confirm the systematic validation approach.

Agreement on claims C51-C52 regarding control experiments for neighboring gene expression. OpenEval explicitly supports these negative controls demonstrating trans-acting mechanism. Peer reviewers do not specifically discuss these controls but raise no concerns, suggesting implicit acceptance.

Perfect agreement on claims C53-C57 regarding arrhythmia susceptibility. Both evaluations support the pathophysiological consequences including enhanced arrhythmia susceptibility and conduction slowing. OpenEval highlights the optical mapping approach while peer reviewers emphasize the clinical relevance for cardiac rhythms.

Agreement on claims C58-C60 regarding functional domain mapping. OpenEval evaluates the deletion mapping separately while peer reviewers group it with the broader conserved fragment findings (C58-C79). Both support the identification of the functional domain, though OpenEval notes C60 could use additional validation.

Strong agreement on claims C61-C72 regarding conserved fragment sufficiency. Both evaluations strongly support that the conserved fragment reproduces full-length phenotypes. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment while peer reviewers describe the conserved segment identification as 'compelling' and highlight its translational relevance.

Agreement on claims C73-C78 regarding in vitro validation of conserved fragment. OpenEval evaluates these in vitro experiments separately while peer reviewers include them in the broader conserved fragment evaluation. Both support the functional validation in cultured cells.

Agreement on claim C79 regarding sequence conservation across species. OpenEval supports the conservation data while noting functional validation in other species would strengthen claims. Peer reviewers implicitly support this through their emphasis on the conserved segment's translational relevance.

Perfect agreement on claims C80-C90 regarding rescue experiments with dystrophin. Both evaluations strongly support these findings as key mechanistic validation. OpenEval describes this as establishing the causal pathway while peer reviewers explicitly list the rescue strategy as a major strength.

Agreement on claims C91-C92 regarding lncDach1 upregulation in heart failure. OpenEval evaluates the disease relevance separately from the Hadhb mechanism while peer reviewers group them together (C91-C102). Both support the pathophysiological relevance and upregulation in heart failure models.

Strong agreement on claims C93-C102 regarding Hadhb regulation of lncDach1. Both evaluations support the upstream regulatory mechanism. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of the mechanistic studies while peer reviewers emphasize the plausible disease mechanism hypothesis. High overlap (83.3% Jaccard) with strong concordance.

Perfect agreement on claims C103-C105 regarding human iPSC-cardiomyocyte validation. Both evaluations support the translational relevance demonstrated in human cells. OpenEval emphasizes the technical challenges and functional effects while peer reviewers implicitly support through emphasis on mammalian conservation.

Strong agreement on overarching conclusions C148-C149. Both evaluations strongly support the main mechanistic conclusions. OpenEval notes these are well-supported by experimental data while peer reviewers emphasize this as first evidence of Nav1.5 regulation by lncRNA and an important contribution to arrhythmia research. OpenEval R18 covers broader background claims (C106-C150) while peer R13 focuses specifically on the main conclusions.
